grants.title: Scaling AI Safety for a Multi-Agent World ($10m funding call)
grants.funder: Schmidt Sciences, LLC administers the fund; programme co-designed with the Cooperative AI…
grants.country: United States / United Kingdom (institutions anywhere in the world may apply)
grants.amount_display: Record's amounts are correct as written. Precise: Tier 1 "Up to US $300,000 (1-2 years)"; Tier 2 "US $300,000-$1,000,000 (1-2…
grants.summary: Two of the four in-scope areas are infrastructure, not theory: 'Sandboxes and Testbeds' (evaluation environments for multi-agent systems) and 'Strengthening Agent Infrastructure'. ArtaQuest is a working, deployed instance of both halves of the problem this call names — it is itself operated by AI agents in the open, and it already enforces the exact property multi-agent safety evaluations lack: that a run is public, that every input is public, that it finished, that it ran with the network off, and that the published artefacts are the ones the run produced, all re-checkable by a third party with no credential. A credible proposal is 'a public, credential-free reproducibility and provenance ledger for multi-agent safety experiments', built on code that already exists and is AGPL-licensed. Crucially for a Canadian charity, this funder does the international-eligibility review ITSELF rather than demanding the applicant arrive with an equivalency determination. EVIDENCE: "Research teams based at institutions anywhere in the world are eligible to apply." and "Applications are due by August 8th, 2026 by 11:59pm AoE" — https://www.cooperativeai.com/grants/multi-agent-safety ; the same programme states organisations must hold "501(c)(3) status or equivalent charitable designation", and that "Schmidt Sciences must evaluate each international direct funding applicant's eligibility for charitable funding under US law, and non-US applicants may be asked to provide specific organizational information".
grants.red_flags: FIVE DAYS to the deadline (8 Aug 2026, 11:59pm AoE) — realistically only attemptable if a proposal can be written immediately, and a rushed Tier 1 bid from an unknown applicant against academic AI-safety labs is a long shot. The scope is foundational SCIENCE on risks from interacting AI agents; reproducibility infrastructure is adjacent, not central, so this is a framing stretch and could read as off-topic. For-profit entities cannot lead a project (fine — ArtaQuest is a charity). The 'or equivalent charitable designation' route means Schmidt Sciences will run its own US-law charitable-funding review on a Canadian registered charity, which adds paperwork and time and can still fail. Awardees announced Autumn 2026, so no money lands this year. ADVERSARIAL VET 2026-08-03: I tried to kill this on all six tests and it survived, though not cleanly. (1) QUOTES ARE REAL. Both sentences the record cites appear verbatim on https://www.cooperativeai.com/grants/multi-agent-safety. No fabrication. (2) CANADIAN CHARITY — THE USUAL KILLER IS AFFIRMATIVELY SOLVED. The page does impose a US-charity test, but it does NOT push equivalency determination onto the applicant. The FAQ "Are there any special requirements for International Direct Awardees?" says Schmidt Sciences "typically achieves this by obtaining an equivalency determination (ED) for each non-US awardee from NGOSource", that it "relies on NGOSource for EDs of its non-US awardees", and that it "will cover the NGOSource costs associated with conducting this initial analysis and any future renewals". That is precisely the brief's carve-out — the funder plainly does ED itself, as routine, at its own expense. A CRA-registered charity is exactly NGOSource's standard case. Non-US bodies may also lead: "Non-U.S.

grants.title: International Grants Program
grants.funder: Taiwan Foundation for Democracy (TFD) — 臺灣民主基金會, Taipei
grants.summary: Non-profit organisations based OUTSIDE Taiwan: 'International non-governmental organizations, academic institutions, think tanks, and other related organizations are eligible to apply.' No country restriction — a Canadian registered charity is an eligible applicant. Open application (not invitation or nomination). Strategic priorities: projects leveraging Taiwan's experience in democracy and human-rights development; projects addressing challenges to democracy and human rights raised by China; projects strengthening democracy and human rights in East Asia (Northeast + Southeast Asia). Funded categories explicitly include 'Educational programs: Enhancing knowledge of democratic and human rights systems, such as through capacity-building and training programs', plus advocacy, research, conferences, and publications 'through print or visual media, for example, through books, articles, and films'. ArtaQuest angle: produce open course series + awareness campaign on democracy and human rights (e.g. Taiwan's democratisation, civic/critical-thinking education for East Asia) — question-first pedagogy is itself democratic capacity-building.
grants.red_flags: Average grant is small (~US$5,000); co-funding expected (no full funding); direct project costs only — NO salaries, honorariums, equipment, or overhead; strategic priorities centre on Taiwan's experience, China-related challenges, and East Asia, so a generic global ed-platform pitch is weak — the proposal must be a concrete democracy/human-rights education project aligned to those priorities; hard-copy application form must physically reach Taipei by the deadline (allow weeks for post); single-calendar-year projects only.

grants.title: Eurofins Foundation project grants — open "Submit a Project" call (applications open March–September each…
grants.country: Belgium (foundation) / Luxembourg (parent group), operating in 60+ countries incl. Canada
grants.amount_display: Cash grant, effectively far below the headline. The €25,000 is a ceiling, but the BINDING limit is the 25% co-funding cap…
grants.summary: On-lane and on-theme: two of the Foundation's four stated funding areas are "Supporting students, especially in STEM education" and "Protecting the environment and biodiversity". ArtaQuest is a free, multilingual open-education platform for reproducible science — a fundable STEM-education project, not a request for corporate marketing. It is the only CASH route I could verify in this lane with an open call, a published cap and a hard, dated deadline five weeks out. Eligibility is stated as legal registration plus track record, with no country bar written anywhere on the page, so a Canadian registered charity is not obviously excluded. EVIDENCE: "Applications are open from March to September each year. The current deadline for applications has been set at 1st September 2026 at 5pm CET." and "Eligibility 1. The organisation implementing the project is legally registered and has an activities track record of at least 24 months; 2. The project is 9-12 months in duration (this period can be part of a multi-year project) and will be implemented between Q4 2026 and Q4 2027" — https://www.eurofins.com/eurofins-foundation/submit-a-project/
grants.red_flags: This is a PROJECT grant, not prize-pool sponsorship: the published exclusions are "Commercial sponsorship requests, sponsoring of sports or cultural events, sponsoring of fundraising activities for NGOs and other charitable causes" — so a member prize pool must not be pitched as sponsorship; it has to be a costed 9–12 month STEM-education project. The grant covers at most 25% of project cost, so ArtaQuest must show the other 75%. Overhead ratio must be under 20% and at most 10% of the grant may go to overheads. One application per organisation per calendar year. No geographic eligibility is stated either way — confirm Canada by email before investing effort. Project must run Q4 2026–Q4 2027. ADVERSARIAL VET 2026-08-02: NOT refuted — a Canadian registered charity has a genuine, open route here, which is rare enough to be worth keeping. This is a Belgian public-interest foundation, so the two gates that kill most corporate-foundation entries for ArtaQuest (US-only eligibility, equivalency determination) are simply absent, and no geography lock is stated. The call is live with a public portal and ~30 days to the deadline. Every sentence the researcher quoted is genuinely on the page. But the proposal is wrong about WHAT ArtaQuest can get, which is why this is caveat and not accept, and why fit is 2/5: 1. OFFER (a) IS EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED. ArtaQuest's cash-into-a-member-prize-pool-for-"Sponsored by"-attribution ask is a "Commercial sponsorship request" — the first item on the exclusion list — and arguably also "sponsoring of ... cultural events". This funder does project grants, not attribution deals. The prize-pool route must be abandoned entirely; only a reframed STEM-education project grant with no quid-pro-quo can be submitted. 2. OFFER (b) IS A NON-ROUTE. Eurofins Scientific is a bioanalytical testing group. There are no software licences, cloud/AI credits, compute or seats to request. Do not list this funder under in-kind. 3.

grants.title: Safeguarding linguistic diversity in Europe (Horizon Europe Cluster 2 call HORIZON-CL2-2026-01-HERITAGE-06)
grants.funder: European Commission — Horizon Europe, the EU's research & innovation framework programme 2021–2027; Pillar II, Cluster 2 'Culture, Creativity and Inclusive Society', Destination 'Innovative Research on European Cultural Heritage and the Cultural an…
grants.country: International — EU programme (Brussels). Projects address Europe's linguistic diversity, but the consortium (and EU funding…
grants.summary: Served community: Europe's REGIONAL, MINORITY and ENDANGERED-LANGUAGE communities (linguistic minorities) and multilingual learners — the topic 'Safeguarding linguistic diversity in Europe' funds work on multilingualism, multilingual education, digital inclusion, language documentation and community-based approaches to sustaining linguistic heritage. Applicants must be a CONSORTIUM, not a single organisation: the standard Horizon Europe Research & Innovation Action rule requires at least three independent legal entities, each established in a different country, with at least one in an EU member state and the others in EU member states and/or Horizon Europe associated countries. ACCESS PATH for ArtaQuest (Canadian charity): Canada has been an ASSOCIATED COUNTRY to Horizon Europe Pillar II since the agreement signed 3 July 2024, so a Canadian organisation can join such a consortium as a FULL, EU-FUNDED beneficiary on equal footing with EU partners (same funding rate; it may even act as coordinator). ArtaQuest's angle: join (or help form) an EU-led consortium as the multilingual-learning technology / civil-society partner, contributing its free, question-first course platform and its ~133-language content-addressed i18n translation mesh to pilot community-driven multilingual education and digital tools for regional/minority/endangered languages — and, in parallel, earmark bursaries (via ArtaQuest's own Grants programme, which directs donations to a learner's group) to learners from those linguistic-minority communities. Consortium partners can be found via the official Net4Society / National Contact Point matchmaking, which already lists this exact topic for partner search.
grants.red_flags: ArtaQuest CANNOT apply alone — every Horizon Europe RIA needs a multi-partner, EU-anchored consortium (≥3 entities from ≥3 EU/associated countries, ≥1 EU member state), so ArtaQuest must join or build one and be one of several beneficiaries, not the sole grantee. It is a RESEARCH & INNOVATION ACTION: the deliverables emphasise documented good practice, rigorous policy-relevant evidence and recommendations on multilingualism, so the consortium typically needs research/academic partners and ArtaQuest would contribute as the technology/platform/community partner rather than lead the science. EU funds cover the project's budgeted activities, not ArtaQuest's general operations and not learner bursaries/regranting (no cascade-funding is foreseen for this topic). The €5–5.75M figure is the EU contribution PER PROJECT shared across all partners — not an amount any single partner receives. The 23 Sep 2026 deadline is a single fixed date within the 2026–2027 Work Programme; the identical topic may not recur in later programmes. Canada's funded participation depends on the Pillar II association staying in force (confirmed active — 2nd EU–Canada Joint Association Committee met in Brussels 26 March 2026), and association covers Pillar II (Cluster 2 sits in Pillar II); Pillar I/III rules differ.

grants.summary: SERVED COMMUNITY: citizens across the EU and associated countries who are vulnerable to disinformation, hybrid threats and civic disengagement — an underrepresented-resilience lever for ArtaQuest's free, multilingual, question-first (critical-thinking) media/information-literacy courses and civic-education content, with learner support earmarkable to the served communities via ArtaQuest's Grants/bursary programme. APPLICANT ELIGIBILITY (official): broad beneficiary types are eligible — associations, educational institutions, NGOs, non-profit organisations, private bodies, research institutions and other legal entities — applying as a CONSORTIUM (Horizon Europe RIA standard: at least three independent legal entities, each established in a different EU member state or Horizon-Europe-associated country). INTERNATIONAL / CANADIAN PATH (verified, DIRECT — axis D): Canada has been associated to Horizon Europe Pillar II (which contains Cluster 2) since the association agreement formalised on 3 July 2024, so a Canadian legal entity such as the ArtaQuest Foundation participates as a FULL beneficiary, receives EU funding at the same rates as EU members, and may even act as coordinator — the only condition (which applies to every participant, EU included) is membership in an eligible consortium. ArtaQuest's realistic role: join, or help assemble, a multi-actor consortium as the multilingual media/digital-literacy LEARNING-PLATFORM and pilot/exploitation partner. No fiscal sponsor or equivalency determination is needed.
grants.red_flags: (1) CONSORTIUM-ONLY: ArtaQuest cannot apply alone — it must join or assemble a multi-actor consortium of at least three independent legal entities from at least three different EU/associated countries, normally with an EU-anchored coordinator; this needs partner-building lead time. (2) RESEARCH-ACTION FRAMING: as an RIA, deliverables are research/innovation outputs — evidence, validated media-literacy tools, pilots and policy recommendations — not core platform-operations money; ArtaQuest's platform would be a means within a research project, not the grant's purpose. (3) NOT REGRANTING/BURSARIES: the grant funds the consortium's own project costs; ArtaQuest's bursary earmarking would be at most a modest work-package, not the grant objective. (4) REIMBURSEMENT + CO-FINANCING CASHFLOW: Horizon grants are paid against milestones/deliverables (100% rate for non-profits, but cashflow and audit/reporting capacity are required). (5) HIGHLY COMPETITIVE: only ~3 projects from the EUR 12M budget. (6) FUNDER ALREADY REPRESENTED: Horizon Europe Cluster 2 already appears in the catalogue (a different destination/topic — Cultural Heritage, and 'Safeguarding linguistic diversity'), so this adds programme depth, not a brand-new funder. (7) ONE-TIME TOPIC: this exact topic closes 23 Sep 2026 and will not necessarily recur in the next work programme — treat as a fixed one-off deadline, not annually recurring.

grants.summary: SERVED COMMUNITY: people in transitional, struggling or closed-space democracies (100+ countries) — civil-society groups, independent media, and citizens exposed to disinformation, censorship and weak civic institutions; an underrepresented-community lever for ArtaQuest (free, multilingual civic-education + media/information-literacy + question-first critical-thinking courses for audiences in those countries, plus learner bursaries earmarked to the served community via ArtaQuest's Grants programme). APPLICANT ELIGIBILITY (official): NED 'only gives grants to organizations' — 'nongovernmental organizations, which may include civic organizations, associations, independent media, and other similar organizations'; it 'does not make grants to individuals, governmental bodies, or state-supported institutions such as public universities'. INTERNATIONAL / CANADIAN PATH (verified, DIRECT): NED 'makes more than 2,000 grants to support the projects of nongovernmental groups abroad ... in more than 100 countries' and, while it 'does not fund democracy-related projects proposing a program implemented in the U.S. or other established democracies', it 'does support organizations based in those countries that work on eligible countries and regions' — so the ArtaQuest Foundation (a Canadian-registered non-profit / NGO, not a state-supported institution) is directly eligible to apply for a project that serves an ELIGIBLE country/region, most competitively co-designed with a local in-country partner (D4 access path). grants.red_flags: (1) GEOGRAPHIC SCOPE: NED does NOT fund projects implemented in the U.S., Canada or other established democracies — ArtaQuest can apply only for a project that serves an ELIGIBLE (transitional/struggling) country or region, so it needs a concrete in-scope country focus (ideally with a local partner) rather than its generic global platform. (2) US-APPROPRIATION RISK: NED is funded principally by an annual U.S. congressional appropriation and its disbursements were temporarily disrupted during the 2025 U.S. funding turbulence; it has since resumed normal grant cycles (its live application calendar shows board decisions scheduled through 11 Sep 2026), but appropriations/political risk to the funding stream is real and worth monitoring. (3) PROJECT, NOT BURSARY REGRANTING: grants fund defined project activities, not unrestricted regranting; ArtaQuest's bursary earmarking would be a modest project component, not the grant's purpose. (4) POLITICAL-PERCEPTION/SAFETY: in authoritarian or NED-hostile states a U.S.-democracy-foundation grant can expose in-country partners to political risk — partner safety must be weighed and the courses must stay genuinely nonpartisan (ArtaQuest's question-first, no-right/wrong, hate-and-fear-filtered model fits this). (5) AMOUNT is modest (avg ~US$50k / 12 months) and not a fixed published range. (6) Next deadline is ESTIMATED (~late Sep 2026) — the confirmed cycle deadlines are 2025-26; verify the next exact date on the official page.

grants.summary: Organisations only — 'foreign national governments, local governments, and other organizations carrying out projects contributing to public interest' (the guidelines state corporate status does not matter); individuals and profit-making corporations cannot apply, and the organisation must be capable of completing the project. SERVED ANGLE + ArtaQuest's mapping: the funded project must both contribute to international understanding AND be 'recognized to have an association with Japan' (eligible-project condition 4), and it must be a discrete project rather than part of the organisation's routine business (condition 7). ArtaQuest's honest, in-scope access angle is therefore a DISCRETE project with a genuine Japan connection — for example, producing free, question-first educational content tied to Japan (Japanese-language localisation of its courses for Japanese learners, or a course on Japanese culture, history or society) that promotes international cultural exchange and goodwill between Japan and the world, in keeping with Expo '70's theme 'Progress and Harmony for Mankind' — drawing on ArtaQuest's Japanese (ja) locale within its 133-language translation mesh. This is a charitable / public-interest grant (no corporate sponsorship and no commercial applicants), and it alternates correctly to a charity after the cycle's two most recent industry-sponsor adds.
grants.red_flags: ASSOCIATION-WITH-JAPAN condition (eligible-project condition 4): the funded project must be recognised to have a genuine connection to Japan, so ArtaQuest must propose a real Japan-linked project (e.g. Japanese-language course localisation or a course on Japanese culture/society), not generic platform support. DISCRETE-PROJECT only (condition 7): the grant cannot fund the organisation's routine or ongoing business; it must be a special, well-defined project. REIMBURSEMENT BASIS (sections 9 and 18): the grant is paid after the project is completed and expenses settled, so the applicant must temporarily front the costs (at most half may be advanced under conditions), and the final amount may be reduced to actual expenses. 75% COVERAGE CAP (section 12): for a Canadian applicant the grant covers at most three-quarters of eligible expenses, requiring at least 25% co-funding, and the applied amount must exceed 5% of the total budget. NO RE-GRANTING / NO FUND-ESTABLISHMENT (condition 11; section 11): the grant cannot be used to establish a fund or to donate acquired property to third parties, so it cannot be passed through as learner bursaries (allows_bursaries_regranting = no). NO RELIGIOUS OR POLITICAL projects (condition 10), and no 'research for the sake of research' (condition 9). NEXT-CYCLE DATE is an estimate: the FY2026 window closed on 30 September 2025 and the exact FY2027 dates are not yet published (official notice expected around July 2026); next_deadline 2026-09-30 is a roll-forward from the consistent recent September pattern and is flagged estimated.

grants.title: ELDP Documentation Grants — competitive grants for the documentation (and community-based revitalisation) of endangered languages worldwide, open to applicants of ANY nationality working through an administering host institution.
grants.funder: Endangered Languages Documentation Programme (ELDP) — the world's flagship international grant programme for endangered-language documentation, founded in 2002 by a donation from the Arcadia Fund (the charitable fund of Lisbet Rausing and Peter…
grants.country: United Kingdom (London) — based at and historically administered through SOAS University of London, funded by the Arcadia…
grants.summary: SERVED COMMUNITY: endangered-language and linguistic-minority communities worldwide (speakers, local scholars, students and community organisations of under-documented / under-resourced languages) — a direct fit for ArtaQuest's free, ~133-language i18n translation mesh and its mission to make knowledge available in every language; ArtaQuest's angle here is a genuine endangered-language documentation project whose corpus and community materials then feed the translation mesh and a set of question-first revitalisation courses in/about the language (course-entry bursaries earmarked to that language community are funded from ArtaQuest's own prize/donation streams, NOT from this grant — ELDP funds documentation activities, not regranting). APPLICANT ELIGIBILITY (official): 'Any individual or group with a keen interest in documenting an endangered language is eligible to apply'; applicants are 'normally expected to have experience in language documentation work, fieldwork, and/or a suitable academic background' ('Anybody with qualifications in linguistic language documentation can apply'). NATIONALITY: no restriction on the PI or the host institution. HOST-INSTITUTION REQUIREMENT (the crux of the access path): 'All grant funds are paid to an accredited institution which administers the grant. Applicants should have, or be in a position to make, a formal link with a university or comparable institution' — the host must be 'a registered entity' with 'experience in administering grants'.
grants.red_flags: (1) CORE PURPOSE IS DOCUMENTATION, not platform-building: ELDP funds the recording, analysis, archiving (and, increasingly, community-based revitalisation) of a specific endangered language — ArtaQuest's learning-platform/i18n angle is a genuine but secondary fit (a documentation project that feeds the mesh + revitalisation courses), hence fit_score 3, not higher. (2) QUALIFIED-PI REQUIREMENT: the Principal Investigator must have language-documentation experience / fieldwork / suitable academic background — ArtaQuest must recruit or partner such a linguist, and that PI may NOT be a director/owner of the host institution. (3) HOST-INSTITUTION GATE: grant funds are paid to an accredited host 'university or comparable institution' that is a registered entity with experience administering grants; a young foundation either must demonstrate that grant-admin capacity itself or affiliate the PI with an established academic host (path is real but must be confirmed per application with eldp@eldp.net). (4) SOME GRANT TYPES ARE INDIVIDUAL-ONLY (Graduate Scholarships, Postdoctoral Fellowships) — out of scope; ArtaQuest targets the Rapid / Small / Major Documentation / Legacy Materials project grants. (5) PROJECT-SPECIFIC, ONE LANGUAGE AT A TIME, and NOT a regranting/bursary vehicle (allows_bursaries_regranting = no). (6) DEPOSIT OBLIGATION: documented materials must be archived in ELAR under ELDP's access/licensing terms.

(https://nserc-crsng.canada.ca/en/funding-opportunity/nserc-awards-science-promotion) — amount: "Individual recipients receive a $10,000 award, and group recipients receive a $25,000 award." (https://nserc-crsng.canada.ca/en/prize/nserc-awards-science-promotion)

Scope risk: the award is framed as 'promotion of science ... encouraging popular interest in science', which is science communication, not research infrastructure — the nomination must be written in NSERC's language (public engagement, science abilities) or it reads as off-topic. Past winners of an NSERC science-promotion award cannot be re-nominated within 10 years (not an issue for us). ADVERSARIAL VET 2026-08-03: Not in the 266-funder catalogue (no NSERC/CRSNG/"Science Promotion" hit in known-funders.json), so no dedupe conflict. So a genuine route exists — but four material conditions, one of which the proposal missed entirely. CAVEAT 1 — THE MONEY IS RESTRICTED, AND RESTRICTED AGAINST EXACTLY WHAT ARTAQUEST IS. The proposal's offer field says only "cash". The sentence immediately after the quoted amount says the funds "must be used in accordance with the PromoScience grants guide", and that guide's live page lists "costs for research" under Ineligible expenses and states twice: "Note that grants may not be used to support research." ArtaQuest is research-reproducibility infrastructure. This $25,000 therefore CANNOT be taken as core/operating support for the platform (ask (a)).

ArtaQuest's contribution is machine-checkable rather than rhetorical — Kaggle's kernels/pull and kernels/output answer with NO credential, so every one of the four public claims (notebook is public, every input is public, the run finished, it ran with the internet switched off) is an assertion a stranger can re-run and contradict. Add the author-only publication gate (an emailed single-use secret plus a device passkey signature mints the DOI; no operator, token or agent can publish) and it is a working demonstration of verifiable research practice, not a policy statement. Self-application is explicit, the award is open worldwide, and there is no US or EU eligibility lock anywhere on the page. EVIDENCE: 'Who can apply: A representative of the institution or organization, such as the Chief Academic Officer, Provost, President or Chancellor.' and 'Researchers and institutions worldwide that are engaged in science, research, education, and scholarship are encouraged to participate in this award.' and 'Submissions for the 2026 award are closed. The next call will open in January 2027.' — all on https://award.einsteinfoundation.de/for-applicants-nominators
grants.red_flags: (1) CLOSED until January 2027 — 'Submissions for the 2026 award are closed. The next call will open in January 2027.' (2) It is a jury PRIZE, not a grant: unplannable, one winner, and 'Award funds must be used solely for scientific purposes' — so it cannot be booked as general operating support and could not legally top up member challenge pools. (3) The institutional category rewards a sustained systemic track record; ArtaQuest's current service is weeks old (reset 2026-07-28) and effectively run by one person plus AI agents, which is a weak fit against university- and national-body-scale competitors. (4) Needs up to three eminent experts external to ArtaQuest willing to be contacted for letters of support — that requires building real standing in the reproducibility community first, which is a 2026 job if the 2027 application is to be credible. (5) The Foundation 'reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to (a) cancel, suspend, or modify the award process, and/or (b) not award prizes if no entries are deemed worthy.' ADVERSARIAL VET 2026-08-03: Every quoted sentence is real and on the stated page, and every hard filter passes: no US 501(c)(3) clause, no equivalency determination, no geography lock (explicitly worldwide), no charitable-status test, an organisation prize rather than an individual fellowship, real cash rather than a discount/affiliate/ad-sale, and an open self-application route that does not require invitation. A Canadian registered charity has a genuine route. Thematic fit is close to ideal: the award is literally for "advancing the rigor, reliability, robustness, and transparency of research", and the recent Institutional winners are reproducibility infrastructure — the Brazilian Reproducibility Initiative (2025), BITSS (2023), the Psychological Science Accelerator (2022). ArtaQuest's ~20-check Kaggle reproducibility gate is the same species of thing. Four material caveats, in order of how much they bite. (1) NOTHING TO SUBMIT TODAY.

grants.summary: ELFA funds a free and open-source, collaborative, decentralised platform — private workspaces plus 'healthy social networking' — built local-first, i.e. it works offline on the device and gains features when connected. ArtaQuest already is a social feed (X-style, hearts only, no downvotes) whose reading, notebook-execution and media surfaces run in the browser: the Pyodide Lab executes notebooks client-side with no server, the Library saves published files to IndexedDB for offline, screen-locked playback, and the JupyterBook view is rendered in the browser from the .ipynb. Those are literally local-first components of a non-extractive social platform, and ELFA's call is for 'auxiliary' efforts aligned with that goal rather than only consortium members. EVIDENCE: "There are no categorical exclusions of persons who may not receive support from ELFA." (https://nlnet.nl/ELFA/eligibility/) — the same page adds that "proposals from outside of those geographic areas can be eligible as well — under the condition that there is a clear European dimension".

Two caveats are material and the pitch understated both. CAVEAT 1 — THE CALL IS NOT OPEN. The pitch's route ("Same NLnet proposal form... choosing the ELFA fund") does not work today. https://nlnet.nl/propose/ states "There are currently no calls open" and ELFA is not mentioned on that page at all; only NGI TALER and NGI Fediversity are live. NLnet paused its NGI Zero calls in June 2026 to "take stock". The reopening is documented and future-dated: "New calls for several funds will open up September 3rd 2026 with a deadline of November 3rd 2026 12:00 CEST (noon)." ELFA is not named in that list, but elfaconsortium.eu corroborates with "Subgranting: opens on 1st September". So the route is real and imminent (~4 weeks), not live. CAVEAT 2 — SCOPE, NOT GEOGRAPHY, IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT.

grants.summary: CodeSupply pays for aggregating and curating software metadata across ecosystems so a consumer can tell what a piece of software is actually built from. ArtaQuest's Kernel checklist does the research-artifact version of that job: for a submitted public Kaggle notebook it resolves every dataSource (datasets, models, other notebooks), records whether each is public, reads the sha256-pinned docker image the run used, and reports whether the run had the internet switched off — then pins the resulting files to a DOI. That is provenance metadata for the scientific software supply chain, produced by a public, re-runnable check rather than a trust assertion, and the checker could be released as a standalone library. EVIDENCE: "Project results shall always become available under a recognised free or open source license." and "Project proposals between 5.000 and 50.000 €" (https://nlnet.nl/codesupply/); the page also states "The first call of CodeSupply will open up soon."

No eligibility page was live for CodeSupply when checked, so the Restack/ELFA 'no categorical exclusions + clear European dimension' rule is assumed, not verified. No call open, no date. Apply here only if the reproducibility checker is spun out as a standalone open-source library. ADVERSARIAL VET 2026-08-03: DEDUPE FLAG FIRST: NLnet Foundation is ALREADY in the 266-entry catalogue twice (store_entries #54 and #119), both `excluded: false`, both for the **NGI Zero Commons Fund**. CodeSupply is a genuinely different, newer programme (separate Horizon Europe grant, separate 400k budget, separate call), so this is a new-programme entry at a known funder, not a duplicate — but it must be filed under the existing NLnet record, not as a 267th funder. TEST 1 — quoted sentences: PASS. "Project results shall always become available under a recognised free or open source license." is verbatim. "The first call of CodeSupply will open up soon." is verbatim. The amount quote is a faithful truncation — the page reads "We are seeking project proposals between 5.000 and 50.000 €." TEST 2 — Canadian charity, not a US 501(c)(3): PASSES CLEANLY. NLnet is a Dutch ANBI; there is no 501(c)(3) clause and no equivalency determination anywhere. Eligibility page: "There are no categorical exclusions of persons who may not receive support from CodeSupply." The submitted brief's claim that "no CodeSupply-specific eligibility page was published" is WRONG — https://nlnet.nl/codesupply/eligibility/ exists and is linked from the nav of the very URL supplied. TEST 3 — organisation vs individual fellowship: PASSES.

TechSoup Canada unlocks the legacy donation catalogue; Goodstack unlocks Google, Anthropic, OpenAI, Twilio, Zoom, Canva, Docusign and Asana. One verification, reused everywhere — so it is a single ~2-3 minute action with the widest downstream payoff in this rail. Confirmed as Canada-capable indirectly but firmly: Google lists Canada as eligible AND mandates Goodstack verification. EVIDENCE: "OpenAI: eligible nonprofits can receive discounts on ChatGPT Team and ChatGPT Enterprise plans" and "Zoom: nonprofits can receive up to 50% off on select Zoom products" (https://goodstack.org/). Canada-capability is established by Google: "All organizations must also be verified as a nonprofit organization by Google for Nonprofits' validation partner Goodstack." https://support.google.com/nonprofits/answer/3215869
grants.red_flags: Goodstack's own homepage never mentions Canada or lists supported countries — Canadian coverage is inferred from Google's page, not stated by Goodstack. Most of what it unlocks is a DISCOUNT, not a donation. Partner list and discount levels change without notice; do not promise a specific vendor rate on the strength of this page. ADVERSARIAL VET 2026-08-02: I tried to refute this and could not. The URL is live, the quoted evidence really is on the page, and the Canada route holds up: Google for Nonprofits mandates Goodstack validation for ALL organizations across 190+ countries including Canada, so Goodstack demonstrably verifies non-US charities and cannot be US-only. No equivalency-determination requirement, no geography lock, no invitation-only or paused language, no dead URL. But the proposal overstates what this is, and three caveats are material: (1) GOODSTACK FUNDS NOTHING. It is verification infrastructure, not a funder. There is no cash, so ArtaQuest's ask (a) — money into a member prize pool — is served at exactly zero. This should sit in the catalogue as an enabling step/infrastructure entry, not as a sponsor that can be approached for a challenge pool. (2) PER-VENDOR GATES SURVIVE VERIFICATION. A Goodstack ID is necessary but not sufficient, and the refutation partially lands here: Asana, listed on the same page, is gated to "nonprofit organizations with 501(c)(3) designation and public libraries with valid nonprofit status" — a US-only gate that a verified Canadian charity still cannot pass. So "verify once, claim everywhere" is wrong; it is "verify once, then re-qualify at each vendor". The realised value for ArtaQuest is unknown until each vendor is checked individually. (3) THE ANTHROPIC QUOTE IS UNCONFIRMED. anthropic.com/nonprofits returns 404 and claude.ai/nonprofits returns 403 (two tries each, then stopped). I could not verify "a quick (~2-3 minute) verification through our partner Goodstack" from any live page.

grants.title: Open Source in Science (Technology programme)
grants.amount_display: Cash grant. Sloan publishes no range for this programme, so use only verified data points: the Canadian precedent in this…
grants.summary: This is the closest thing in world philanthropy to a funder whose stated purpose is ArtaQuest. The programme explicitly does NOT fund individual open-source dev projects; it funds 'tooling, institutions, economic models, and incentives around the production, maintenance, and adoption of research software' — i.e. the layer ArtaQuest occupies. Its 'Publication & Archiving' focus area names exactly what the platform does: software that is 'uncited, poorly archived, difficult to reuse, and poorly integrated into the scholarly communication system', and seeks 'efforts that aim to elevate software as a first-order research product as well as efforts that aim to improve code review and the linkages between software and other research outputs, such as articles, preprints, or data'. ArtaQuest's ~20 credential-free reproducibility checks against Kaggle's public API, the Zenodo DOI minted to the notebook's AUTHOR (not the submitter), and the Library that makes published output files re-attachable are all 'linkage between software and other research outputs' made machine-checkable. Pitch it as scholarly infrastructure with a public assertion anyone can re-run, not as a website. EVIDENCE: "Apply — Interested grantseekers should send a two-page letter of inquiry to technology@sloan.org." and "Rather than funding individual open source development projects, grants in this area focus mainly on tooling, institutions, economic models, and incentives around the production, maintenance, and adoption of research software, hardware, models, and other related research outputs." — both on https://sloan.org/programs/digital-technology/open-source-in-science . Non-US precedent in this same sub-programme: "City Montréal, Canada, Canada … Sub-program Better Software for Science" (now renamed Open Source in Science), a $382,020 grant funding "Jin Guo of McGill University and Jinghui Cheng of Polytechnique Montréal" — https://sloan.org/grant-detail/9591 .
grants.red_flags: (1) Sloan is a US private foundation, so a grant to a Canadian registered charity runs through expenditure responsibility or equivalency determination — Sloan does not advertise this as a barrier and plainly funds foreign institutions (Montréal grant above), but the Canadian precedent I found is a UNIVERSITY, not an independent charity; ask the programme officer directly in the first email. (2) The programme is oriented toward the academic research enterprise — a platform with no university anchor is unusual for them; a named academic co-applicant or letters of support from researchers who have submitted notebooks would materially de-risk the LOI. (3) sloan.org blocks automated fetching (Cloudflare 403 to both WebFetch and curl) — I read every quote above through the r.jina.ai text proxy; re-check in a browser before sending. (4) Same LOI inbox as the Exploratory Grantmaking candidate below — pick ONE programme, do not send two. ADVERSARIAL VET 2026-08-03: I tried to refute this and could not. Every quoted sentence is real and still live today, and the load-bearing Canadian precedent checks out exactly as described. Note on access: sloan.org sits behind a Cloudflare interstitial — WebFetch 403'd twice and plain curl 403'd. I verified via (a) the Wayback snapshot of 2026-05-24 and (b) a live text-proxy read of the raw HTML today, which returned the Apply markup verbatim. Both agree. TEST 1 — sentences appear: PASS. All quoted text is verbatim, including the email, which is Cloudflare-obfuscated on the page (I decoded `data-cfemail` to `technology@sloan.org` and separately saw it in cleartext in the live raw HTML). TEST 2 — Canadian charity, not a US 501(c)(3): PASS, and this is the strong part. I read the complete "What We Do Not Fund" list and the whole grant-application section. There is no 501(c)(3) clause, no US-only clause, no equivalency-determination requirement and no geography lock anywhere. The only entity-type bar is for-profits.

grants.summary: The single best-worded match found anywhere in this search: the AI in Science focus area lists as a current interest 'reproducibility and transparency of machine learning-enabled science'. That is a one-line description of ArtaQuest's gate — is the notebook public, is every input public, did the run finish, did it run with the internet switched off — asserted from Kaggle's public API so a stranger can contradict it with no credential. This programme also funds precisely the shape of thing ArtaQuest is at this stage: 'early technology development and prototyping', 'development of protocols and standards', 'initial research on and engagement with potential user communities', and 'demonstration or other proof-of-concept projects', in areas 'for which public or private funding is scarce or unavailable'. Frame the ask as standardising a re-runnable reproducibility assertion for ML-enabled work, with the running platform as the demonstrator. EVIDENCE: "AI in Science — The complexity and opacity of AI-driven research methods has raised new questions about the degree to which their results can or should be trusted to advance scientific research. Current areas of interest include: reproducibility and transparency of machine learning-enabled science; ways that the philosophy of science and related fields might help to inform the optimal uses of machine learning to produce new knowledge; and the relative value of foundation models vs. good old fashioned machine learning for scientific discovery." and "Apply — Interested grantseekers should email a letter of inquiry of no more than two pages to [address masked by the text renderer; the sibling Technology programme page gives technology@sloan.org]." — https://sloan.org/programs/digital-technology/exploratory-grantmaking-in-technology
grants.red_flags: (1) Same programme staff and same LOI inbox as Open Source in Science — these are ONE relationship; choose the programme that fits the ask and say why. Open Source in Science suits a core-infrastructure ask; Exploratory suits a bounded prototype/standards ask. (2) 'Exploratory' means small, time-boxed, evidence-gathering grants — do not ask for operating support here. (3) Both listed recent grants are US universities; the same expenditure-responsibility question as above applies. (4) Quotes read via r.jina.ai because sloan.org 403s automated fetches; the apply email address on THIS page was masked by the renderer and must be confirmed manually. ADVERSARIAL VET 2026-08-03: Survives every refutation test I could mount, but not cleanly enough for a bare accept. 1. QUOTE — verified verbatim, both passages, word for word including "good old fashioned machine learning". The BU $399,297 and UND $125,000 figures are also exact. Nothing was embellished. 2. ELIGIBILITY — the real test, and it passes. Sloan's "What We Do Not Fund" list has eight exclusions and NOT ONE is a US-only, 501(c)(3), or tax-exempt clause; no equivalency determination is mentioned anywhere in the public application guidelines. Better than an absence of prohibition, I found affirmative proof of cross-border grantmaking on Sloan's own grant record: University of British Columbia, City "Vancouver, BC", $25,000, 2020. Sloan grants directly to Canadian organisations. 3. ORGANISATION, not individual — "The Foundation does not make grants to individuals except through its Books program." ArtaQuest Foundation qualifies. (The "Metascience & AI Postdoctoral Fellows" banner on the same page IS individual-only — it is a different, irrelevant route. Do not confuse them.) 4. REAL MONEY — an unrestricted cash grant. Not a discount, not affiliate, not an ad desk. 5. OPEN — the Apply section actively solicits inquiries, with no pause or invitation-only language. Snapshot is one day old.

The github.com/nonprofit URL 301s twice (via socialimpact.github.com) before landing, and the landing page is thin on process; expect to negotiate by email rather than self-serve. Enterprise is a discount, not a donation. ADVERSARIAL VET 2026-08-02: I tried to refute this on all seven vectors and it survived. (1) The evidence sentence IS on the page — their quote was truncated mid-sentence but faithful, not fabricated. So a Canadian charity has a genuine route, and ArtaQuest already satisfies the first requirement (an existing GitHub org). Four material conditions, hence the caveat rather than a clean accept. First and most serious: eligibility requires the org be "non-academic" and "non-commercial". ArtaQuest is an open-education and research platform whose org bio literally reads "social media for science and education", and it runs entry-fee challenges and a /shop. It is a charity, not an academic institution, so it should read as eligible — but this is the one live refusal vector, and it is a reviewer's judgement call, not something the page settles. Lead the application with "Canadian registered charity, not a school or university" and the CRA number. Second: this is a discount and a free tier, not a donation — it does nothing for offer (a), the cash prize pool.

Fit is also real rather than nominal: a CDN/edge grant directly addresses a known live problem, since ArtaQuest's media CDN path (pub-*.r2.dev) is blackholed at TLS on ordinary networks and media currently falls back to origin uploads. Two material caveats, which is why this is not a clean 'accept': 1. IN-KIND ONLY, AND POSSIBLY A DISCOUNT. The page says "free and discounted services" — both words. ADVERSARIAL VET 2026-08-03: Every eligibility claim survived adversarial testing, and this is a genuinely rare find: a large funder with an always-open form, no US-501(c)(3) clause anywhere on the page, and explicit worldwide charity eligibility. I grepped the full application page for "501", "equivalen", "IRS" and "tax-deduct" — ZERO hits. There is no US-only requirement and no equivalency determination. ArtaQuest Foundation, being CRA-registered, satisfies "must already have charity status" directly and needs no fiscal sponsor. It is an organisation grant, not an individual fellowship (individuals are explicitly excluded unless fiscally sponsored). It is real cash from Jaan Tallinn — not a discount, affiliate scheme or ad-sales desk. The /rolling-application 307 redirect to the Google Form is live: I confirmed the Location header myself today (response "date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026").

grants.title: Drosos Foundation — project funding via the foundation's open, ROLLING 'Partner with us / Funding request' channel (no fixed deadline; funding requests accepted year-round).
grants.funder: Drosos Foundation (Drosos Stiftung) — an independent, non-profit private foundation headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland, that works to enable people living in disadvantaged circumstances — especially children, young people and young adults — to…
grants.country: Switzerland (HQ) — funding two clusters: EUROPE (Switzerland, Eastern Germany) and the MENA region (Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon…
grants.amount_display: Per-grant / per-project amounts are NOT publicly disclosed: the official drosos.org pages do not publish grant sizes, and the…
grants.summary: ELIGIBLE APPLICANTS: LOCAL not-for-profit organisations based in Drosos's focus countries — in Europe (Switzerland, Eastern Germany) and the MENA region (Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, Morocco, Palestine, Tunisia; historically also Syria) — that work directly with disadvantaged children, young people and young adults on access to education, creative & cultural activities, vocational/technical & life skills, social development, youth empowerment and economic independence. Drosos 'supports local organisations that work closely with young people and their communities' and 'encourage[s] applications from young and emerging organisations with innovative approaches'. NOT eligible: individual requests, emergency aid, and anything outside Drosos's regional & thematic focus. SERVED COMMUNITY / ARTAQUEST ANGLE: disadvantaged MENA youth — ArtaQuest's eligible access path is axis-D(4): co-apply with / support a LOCAL MENA partner organisation (the lead grantee) on a project that uses ArtaQuest's free, Arabic & multilingual, question-first learning platform plus course-entry bursaries earmarked to that community's young people, with ArtaQuest providing the platform, localised content and capacity support. ArtaQuest itself, as a Canadian organisation, cannot be the direct grantee — the local partner is.
grants.red_flags: (1) NO DIRECT CANADIAN PATH — Drosos funds LOCAL organisations in its focus countries, so ArtaQuest can access this only via a local MENA partner organisation as the lead grantee (axis D4); ArtaQuest's role is platform/content/capacity partner, not the direct recipient. (2) AMOUNTS NOT DISCLOSED — neither the official site nor the (paywalled) DARPE directory publishes per-grant sizes; recorded as null rather than invented. (3) PARTNERSHIP-/RELATIONSHIP-ORIENTED + SELECTIVE — Drosos develops projects collaboratively and only responds to requests that strongly align with its regional and thematic focus; a cold concept note must fit tightly. (4) PROJECT-DIRECTED, multi-year programme funding — not unrestricted operating money and not a third-party regranting/bursary vehicle (bursaries can only be a funded sub-component delivered by the local partner), hence allows_bursaries_regranting recorded 'no'. (5) FOCUS-COUNTRY RESTRICTED — only the listed Europe + MENA countries qualify; no emergency aid, no individual requests. (6) OFFICIAL SITE BOT-BLOCKED — drosos.org returns HTTP 403 to automated fetch, so facts were corroborated from the official 'Partner with us / Funding request' page content surfaced via search plus Wikipedia, the DARPE MENA development directory and Devex; re-confirm details directly on drosos.org before applying.

grants.title: JetBrains s.r.o. — Community Support Program, open-source licence track
grants.country: Netherlands (group HQ, Amsterdam) / Czech Republic (Prague, s.r.o.); tracks open worldwide
grants.amount_display: No cash route. In-kind only, and the licences are non-transferable, so they can never be prizes.
grants.summary: JetBrains s.r.o. is the privately held maker of the IntelliJ-platform developer tools — IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, PhpStorm, GoLand, Rider, CLion, RubyMine, DataGrip and the ReSharper/.NET tools — plus the Kotlin language and YouTrack, TeamCity and SpaceCode (Space was rebranded SpaceCode in May 2024; Fleet was discontinued in 2025). Founded in Prague in 2000, privately held, never externally funded. Its Community Support Program gives free product licences on four tracks: non-commercial open-source projects, user groups and developer communities, content creators, and recognised industry experts. The track ArtaQuest could plausibly use is open source — free All Products Pack licences for the named, active maintainers of a publicly available repository under a recognised OSS licence, with JetBrains auto-checking that new code was submitted every month over the past three months (documentation-only and Dependabot commits do not count) and granting only to contributors whose work is regular and visible. The route is geography-free: no charity registration, fiscal sponsor or equivalency determination is involved. What ArtaQuest would actually receive is professional IDE seats for its own maintainers — genuinely useful for a code-heavy open platform, but nothing that reaches members.
grants.red_flags: There is no cash route at all. The events-partnership sponsorship_request.html form this record was built on now 302s to /community/user-groups/, and JetBrains' guidance reserved financial support for physical IT conferences of roughly 300+ attendees hosting a JetBrains booth — a bar an online platform cannot meet. The licences cannot be prizes: the open-source subscription is non-transferable, forbids providing a third party with access to the Product, and is restricted to developing the applicant's own non-commercial project, so awarding one to a competition winner would breach the agreement that granted it. The only track that permits raffling licences is User Groups, which requires monthly in-person meetings averaging 30+ attendees. Much of the value is commoditised: since 2024-25 IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, Rider and RubyMine are free for non-commercial use with no application. Whether ArtaQuest's repository is public and OSS-licensed with monthly commits is unconfirmed. Due diligence: the 2021 TeamCity/SolarWinds press episode (JetBrains denied involvement); Russian sales suspended 2022, Russian entity liquidated 2023.

grants.title: GEF Small Grants Programme (SGP) — community grants, Eighth Operational Phase (OP8). The GEF SGP, a corporate programme of the Global Environment Facility implemented by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), finances community-led…
grants.funder: The Global Environment Facility (GEF) Small Grants Programme (SGP), implemented by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) — a GEF corporate programme operating since 1992 that channels small grants directly to civil-society and community-bas…
grants.country: Global / Global South (UN — GEF/UNDP corporate programme). Grants are awarded ONLY to organisations registered and operatin…
grants.summary: WHO IS ELIGIBLE: local / national civil-society organisations — NGOs, community-based organisations (CBOs) and grassroots groups — that are duly registered and operating in an SGP-participating country; the programme explicitly prioritises empowering poor and vulnerable communities, including INDIGENOUS PEOPLES, WOMEN, YOUTH and PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES. The proposed project must correspond to a GEF focal area (biodiversity, climate change, land degradation / sustainable land management, international waters, chemicals & waste) and generate global environmental benefits through community-led action; eligible activity types explicitly include access to knowledge and information, learning-by-doing, skill development, awareness-raising and capacity-building. An organisation based in a non-participating donor country (e.g. a Canadian charity) CANNOT be the direct grantee. ARTAQUEST FIT / ANGLE (the standard thematic-fund model — produce courses + an awareness campaign on the fund's mission): partner with an in-country CBO/NGO that leads an SGP project, and contribute free, question-first environmental-education courses (climate, biodiversity, sustainable-land-management or pollution / chemicals-and-waste literacy) in the community's language via the ~133-language mesh, plus course-access bursaries earmarked to that community, as the knowledge / awareness / capacity-building component of the project. ACCESS PATH: local partner leads as grantee; ArtaQuest is the education / technology partner (it cannot apply solo).
grants.red_flags: (1) NO DIRECT CANADIAN / DONOR-COUNTRY PATH — the applicant must be a national CSO/CBO/NGO registered and operating in an SGP-participating (mostly Global-South) country; ArtaQuest can only join via a local partner that leads the project (it cannot be the grantee or apply solo). (2) ENVIRONMENTAL FOCAL-AREA MANDATE — projects must generate global environmental benefits (biodiversity / climate / land / international waters / chemicals); ArtaQuest qualifies only via the environmental-education / awareness / capacity-building component of a community environmental project, not via its general learning mission (thematic stretch). (3) COUNTRY-SPECIFIC PERIODIC / ROLLING CALLS — no single global deadline; each country's National Coordinator runs its own Call for Proposals on its own schedule (recorded deadline_type rolling, next_deadline null, confidence low — no date invented). (4) SUB-COMPONENT ROLE, NOT REGRANTING — the grant (up to USD 30,000 for CBO/groups, up to USD 50,000 for NGOs) goes to the local partner; ArtaQuest's courses + bursaries are a budget line within the partner's project, not a prime award or a regranting vehicle. (5) COMPETITIVE + COUNTRY-QUOTA-LIMITED — concept papers are screened and selected by the National Steering Committee within each country's allocation. (6) REQUIRES A GENUINE IN-COUNTRY PARTNER — ArtaQuest needs a real, registered local CBO/NGO partner in an eligible country to anchor any application.

grants.title: Hugging Face — Community GPU Grant, requested from a Space's hardware settings
grants.country: United States (HQ Manhattan, New York City); global open platform, no geographic restriction
grants.amount_display: No cash. In-kind compute only: Community GPU Grants, explicitly revocable, with no published value.
grants.summary: Hugging Face, Inc. is the American open-source AI company behind the Hugging Face Hub, the platform where the machine-learning community collaborates on models, datasets and applications — over 2 million models, 500,000+ datasets, 1 million+ Spaces and 50,000+ organisations — and the maintainer of Transformers, Diffusers, Datasets, Tokenizers, PEFT, Accelerate and TRL. Founded 2016 by Clément Delangue (CEO), Julien Chaumond (CTO) and Thomas Wolf (CSO); headquartered in Manhattan, New York City. The one mechanism by which Hugging Face actually transfers value on application is a Community GPU Grant, requested from a Space's own hardware settings and documented at huggingface.co/docs/hub/spaces-gpus: self-serve, geography-blind, and open to any Space owner including a Canadian charity. Around it sit free public tiers that anyone may use — Hugging Face for Classrooms (free collaborative classroom workspaces for students and teachers), the Learn courses, the open education toolkit for universities, and the community forum and Discord. ArtaQuest already publishes models and datasets to Hugging Face, so this is a warm existing relationship rather than a cold prospect, and the Hub's public, versioned artefacts sit directly on the platform's reproducible-research purpose.
grants.red_flags: AUDIT CORRECTION 2026-08-02: an earlier draft of this row carried '$0.40-$23.50/hr' in the amount column. That is Hugging Face's PRICE LIST for hardware ArtaQuest would buy, not the value of anything granted, and it is removed. No cash exists anywhere in this entry: everything on offer is compute, hosting and visibility, never a contribution to a prize pool. There is no sponsorship programme — no 'apply to sponsor' channel, no nonprofit tier, no published partnerships route for a charity — so any brand relationship would be cold outreach. The old record built its case on Classrooms, Learn and Hub hosting, which are free to literally everybody; receiving a public free tier is not a sponsorship and buys no attribution. Free hosting is now qualified: CPU Basic has no hourly cost, but creating a new Space that runs on compute (Gradio or Docker) requires a paid plan, and only static Spaces are free for everyone. GPU grants are explicitly revocable — 'provided temporarily and might be removed after some time if the usage is very low'. The Student Ambassador Program must be dropped from the access path: the only official announcement (13 May 2022) closed applications on 13 June 2022 and the cohort ended 31 December 2022. huggingface.co/learn lists twelve courses but carries no explicit 'free' statement, so that word is true in practice yet not quotable from the page.

grants.title: Mapbox Community / nonprofit support programme
grants.amount_display: In-kind only — donated or discounted Mapbox map/location product, plus technical guidance and promotion. No dollar figure…
grants.summary: Maps and geography are the 'travel/geography' half of this lane, and the gift is exactly the kind ArtaQuest can use: map/API credits that members' reproducible Kaggle notebooks can render geospatial results with, and that the platform could use for a geography-themed member challenge. The programme is explicitly for nonprofits, is applied to by an open form rather than by invitation, and runs on published review cycles — so an unsolicited approach from a Canadian charity is the intended behaviour, not an exception. Cash into a prize pool is NOT on offer here; this is an in-kind ask only. EVIDENCE: "Product donations, discounts, and account help." … "Applications are reviewed in May and November." … "If approved, begin receiving support in July or January, depending on cohort." — https://www.mapbox.com/community
grants.red_flags: The page does not publish eligibility criteria (no statement on country, charity-registration type, or revenue caps), so Canadian eligibility is inferred from the absence of any US-only wording rather than confirmed — ask in the form. Support arrives in cohorts (July or January), so this is a 6-12-month lead-time ask, not a fast one. Students and academic research projects are pushed to a separate education page, so the request must be framed as the charity's own platform need, not as research. No cash route exists here at all. ADVERSARIAL VET 2026-08-02: I could not refute this on eligibility, and I tried every gate on the list. https://www.mapbox.com/community loads, the programme is active, and all three of the researcher's quoted sentences appear on the page verbatim. There is NO US-only restriction, NO 501(c)(3) requirement, NO equivalency-determination requirement, NO geography lock, and no invitation-only language anywhere on the page. "Discount not donation" is also refuted: the page says "donated or discounted services", so donations are genuinely on the table (though the award mix is at Mapbox's discretion and unstated). A Canadian registered charity is not excluded by anything published. The application Google Form is live (6 pages, opens with a required email field) — not closed. So the hard-gate tests all come back clean and refuted=false. The proposal fails on two material conditions the researcher did not surface, which is why this is caveat and not accept. CAVEAT 1 — a usage precondition ArtaQuest does not currently meet. The application is not open-ended goodwill; step 2 is explicitly conditional: "If usage exceeds free tiers, apply for support." Step 1 tells you to build first. ArtaQuest has zero Mapbox usage and no geospatial surface — it is a Kaggle-notebook reproducibility feed. The award is Mapbox map/location product, so there is presently nothing to ask for and nothing an award would pay for.

grants.title: Esri Nonprofit Organization Program
grants.country: United States (programme administered outside the US by the local Esri office — for ArtaQuest, Esri Canada)
grants.amount_display: In-kind only — a 50–99% DISCOUNT on ArcGIS software/subscriptions (a purchase, not donated licences)…
grants.summary: Geography/mapping sits squarely in this lane, and this is the rare programme that names a non-US path explicitly rather than defaulting to a US-only 501(c)(3) test — which matters because ArtaQuest is a Canadian registered charity and is disqualified by most US corporate nonprofit programmes on the first line. The gift is ArcGIS software, training and content, which maps onto member notebooks that publish geospatial datasets and figures, and onto a geography/world-culture challenge topic. Note this is a DISCOUNT programme, not a donation programme, and there is no prize-pool cash route. EVIDENCE: "The Esri Nonprofit Organization Program provides nonprofit organizations with low-cost access to GIS software, training, content, and other resources." (https://www.esri.com/en-us/industries/nonprofit/overview) and, on the programme page, "Outside the US, requirements are set by the local Esri office or distributor." plus "Organizations will be reviewed by the local Esri office or distributor and will not need to complete verification with TechSoup." — https://www.esri.com/en-us/industries/nonprofit/nonprofit-program
grants.red_flags: This is discounted, not free — ArtaQuest would still pay something, and the actual Canadian price and terms are set by Esri Canada, which publishes none of them on this page, so the real cost is unknown until contact is made. The programme page's stated exclusions are written against US categories (it excludes "hospitals and health-care systems, governmental entities, schools and academic institutions, and commercial organizations"), and whether Esri Canada applies the same list is unverified. Zero cash: nothing here can fund a member prize pool. Fit depends on ArtaQuest actually wanting GIS in member notebooks — if no member is publishing geospatial work, the licence is dead weight. ADVERSARIAL VET 2026-08-02: I could not refute the eligibility claim — every geography-based refutation fails. The page scopes 501(c)(3) explicitly and only to US applicants ("for US nonprofit organizations, 501(c)(3) status is required"), invites the world ("Organizations of all sizes, from around the world, are invited to apply"), cites reach "across 126 countries", requires no equivalency determination, and explicitly exempts non-US applicants from TechSoup. The programme is live (HTTP 200, "Apply Now", "more than 17,000 organizations"), not paused or invitation-only, and all three sentences the researcher quoted appear verbatim. So a Canadian registered charity does have a genuine route — hence not a reject. It is accept-with-caveat, not accept, on four material conditions the proposal understates: (1) DISCOUNT, NOT DONATION — this is the decisive one. The proposal's "in-kind" framing reads as free licences. The page is a purchase-discount catalogue end to end: hero "Discounted offers on software, training, and content", "The world's most powerful GIS software at a discounted price", "low-cost access", "discounted 50–99%".

grants.title: Localazy for Nonprofits (free basic accounts) + Ambassador Program for higher tiers
grants.amount_display: In-kind only, and effectively unquantified. The nonprofit page promises "basic Localazy accounts for free to get started"…
grants.summary: The single most directly usable in-kind gift in this lane for ArtaQuest specifically: the platform already runs a ~133-language translation mesh, so a localization-management account is a tool it would use on day one rather than a nice-to-have. Translation is named in the lane, and language/mother-tongue is already an ArtaQuest competition topic. Eligibility is stated as "worldwide", with no US-charity test, which is unusual and suits a Canadian charity. Weakest of the three on money: this is a small company, the free tier is explicitly "basic", and there is no sponsorship or cash route on the page at all. EVIDENCE: "We are happy to support some of the most popular nonprofit causes and projects worldwide as well as social enterprises." and "To help you spread positive impact across the world and make your solutions globally available, we are proud to support you with basic Localazy accounts for free to get started." — https://localazy.com/for/nonprofit (same wording also appears on https://localazy.com/pricing)
grants.red_flags: Vaguest route of the three: the nonprofit page has no application form, no eligibility test, no stated approval process, and no published limits — everything is decided in an email thread, which means it could quietly amount to nothing. "Basic accounts" is likely far below what a 133-language mesh needs, and the page pushes larger needs into an Ambassador Program that is earned by contributing points, i.e. it costs ArtaQuest labour rather than being a gift. Small private company: no realistic prospect of cash for a member prize pool. Also verify before pitching that ArtaQuest actually wants a third-party TMS in the loop, given the mesh already persists translations into the public aq_translations table. ADVERSARIAL VET 2026-08-02: The refutation attempt FAILED on every hard-gate test, so this is not rejectable: the URL is live, the programme shows no pause/closure notice, and both evidence sentences are on the page verbatim. Critically for ArtaQuest, there is NO US-only clause, NO 501(c)(3) requirement, NO equivalency-determination requirement, NO charity-registry proof demanded and NO geography lock — the vendor is Czech, not American, and its own wording is "worldwide". A Canadian charity is not excluded by anything written. Hence refuted=false and a route genuinely exists. But the caveat is material and it is the whole story. THE MATERIAL CONDITION: the "donation" is not shown to exceed the public free tier. "Basic accounts for free" maps to a Free plan that is already $0, already self-serve, and already "Unlimited seats & languages" for anyone — the nonprofit page adds no stated uplift. Its hard ceiling is 200 source keys. ArtaQuest's content-addressed i18n mesh across ~133 languages will blow through 200 source keys immediately, so the free grant is functionally decorative at our volume.

grants.title: Nonprofit licensing — free weather data and weather API access for qualifying nonprofit organisations
grants.amount_display: In-kind only — free nonprofit licence covering historical weather data, forecast data, data download and the weather API.
grants.summary: The exchange terms are almost exactly ArtaQuest's ask: value given for attribution only, nothing else — "In exchange for this free access to our data service, we ask that you place a link to Visual Crossing somewhere on your website indicating that you use our data in your work." No editorial control, no data about members, no fee. Weather and climate are a live ArtaQuest surface (ArtaNews signals, climate/seasonality topics) and a natural challenge theme, and the route is two low-friction steps a single person can complete in an afternoon. Marked 3 because the in-kind value is modest and the reproducibility caveat below is real. EVIDENCE: "As a part of our commitment to our community, Visual Crossing is pleased to offer free access to our data and APIs for qualifying nonprofit organizations. If you work with or know of a nonprofit in need of weather data or a weather API, please let us know and we will work with you to find the best plan." — https://www.visualcrossing.com/resources/documentation/weather-data/weather-data-and-weather-apis-for-nonprofit-organizations/
grants.red_flags: Reproducibility clash worth naming up front: an API key is a credential, and ArtaQuest's own Kernel checklist BLOCKS a notebook that needs one — so this cannot be a member-notebook input. It fits platform-side use, or ArtaQuest publishing an openly-licensed derived dataset that members then build on (needs their written sign-off on redistribution). "qualifying nonprofit organizations" is never defined and no country is mentioned, so Canadian eligibility is genuinely unknown. Standard licence carries "a strict commercial use restriction". The article is dated 7 June 2022 though the site footer is 2026 — treat the programme as live but confirm in the first email. Attribution link on artaquest.com is a condition, not optional. ADVERSARIAL VET 2026-08-02: I tried to refute this and could not. Every hard gate I was asked to test for is absent from the live page: no mention of the United States, 501(c)(3), tax-exempt status, charity registration, equivalency determination, or any country/geography restriction; it is described as free access, not a discount; it is open self-serve application, not invitation-only; the page is live today (2026-08-02, "© 2026 All rights reserved") and the URL resolved cleanly on two separate fetches. Both sentences the researcher quoted appear verbatim — the evidence holds. So a Canadian registered charity has a genuine, unblocked route to apply, and the proposal's core claim survives. It is NOT an accept, for two reasons the proposal missed.

grants.title: Zoho for Nonprofits — one-time wallet credit covering up to 50% of subscription cost across Zoho products
grants.country: India / United States (HQ not stated on the fetched page — unconfirmed)
grants.amount_display: Up to $5,000 wallet credit (in-kind, non-cash) — NOT $5,000 of free software.
grants.summary: Lane hook is Zoho's finance and hiring stack — Zoho Books, Invoice, Expense, Payroll (accounting) and Zoho Recruit / Zoho People (career & hiring). For ArtaQuest specifically this is operational in-kind support a one-person charity can actually consume: books and expense tracking behind the public financial-transparency page, and forms/CRM for the donations and challenge-sponsor pipeline. The route is open right now, rolling, with no cycle to wait for, and Canada is named explicitly as a jurisdiction that can apply DIRECTLY (no TechSoup intermediary), so a CRA charity registration is sufficient documentation. Honest limit: this is credits against ArtaQuest's own software bill, not cash for a member prize pool. EVIDENCE: "That's why we're offering nonprofit organizations a one-time $5,000 credit to use across Zoho products." and "If you are from India, Australia, New Zealand, the UK, USA, or Canada, you also have an option to apply directly by sharing the required local documents." — both https://www.zoho.com/nonprofits/
grants.red_flags: Zoho is a broad business-software suite, not a fintech — the money/work/career hook is its accounting (Books/Payroll/Expense) and hiring (Recruit/People) products, so another lane could plausibly claim this company. The credit only pays half of each transaction, so it requires matched spend by ArtaQuest. Some products are excluded (Zoho Voice, Zoho Sign API, Zoho Domains, ManageEngine). No cash and no "Sponsored by" attribution route — this is a nonprofit-tier plan only. Legal entity name and HQ were not stated on the fetched page. ADVERSARIAL VET 2026-08-02: The claim survives adversarial vetting: I could not find a hard gate.
